_propertySchemaComment: Single source of truth for the per-model property filter columns, mirrored by both the interactive map (index.html reads data.propertySchema) and the per-model pages (tools/gen-pages.py). Each group has a display heading, a sub-label, and an ordered list of [key, label] field pairs; the key indexes into modelProperties. Grouped as in Tables 1–2 of Moiseenko et al., 'A Survey of Programming Language Memory Models' (2021), except Atomicity (Su & Colvin 2026, §2.4) and the Inverse roach motel column (Poetzl & Kroening 2015; see propertyProvenance).
_propertyProvenanceComment: Per-property (column) provenance. The default source for the property columns is the Moiseenko–Podkopaev–Koznov survey (Tables 1–2); this map records only the columns whose definition/data come from a different source, so a reader knows a given cell is not survey-tabulated even when the per-model modelPropertyProvenance says 'survey'. Absence here = the survey default.

propertyProvenance.irm: Inverse (reversed) roach motel reordering — moving a shared access out of a critical section. Not tabulated by the Moiseenko et al. survey; the transformation and its soundness for the SC-for-DRF execution model were introduced by Poetzl & Kroening, 'Formalizing and Checking Thread Refinement for Data-Race-Free Execution Models' (arXiv:1510.07171, 2015), §4. The 'yes' cells are therefore author-assigned to the SC-preserving / SC-for-DRF models on the strength of that result, not taken from the survey.
propertyProvenance.mca: Multicopy atomicity — not from the Moiseenko et al. survey but from Su & Colvin, 'Weak Memory Model Formalisms: Introduction and Survey' (Concurrency Comput. Pract. Exper. 38(2), 2026), §2.4.
